name: Amazon Ancient Ruins
status: v0.6.1 geometry rebaseline before further exactification
notes: V0.6.1 deliberately stops trusting the old presentation scaffold while preserving already proven instruction transforms.

The single molded 30271px1 inventory baseplate is now represented as a low shell plus 22 render-only terrain-mold helpers that create a deep central river channel and four corner pits; the helpers are explicitly excluded from the 420-part ledger.
The baseplate catalog envelope is 32 x 48 x 6 bricks high, so the river is lowered to the channel rather than floating at the old near-flat base elevation.
The rope bridge presentation is corrected to its real 16 x 4 footprint. The previous data orientation exercised a renderer path that effectively made the bridge roughly 16 studs wide.
Boat hull 33129 is corrected from an undersized 6 x 12 x 1.5 proxy to an 8 x 18 x 4 world-unit envelope corresponding to the catalog 18 x 8 x 3 1/3-stud hull and is lowered into the river.

The off-road car body remains deliberately non-exact. Its questionable reconstruction pieces are tagged presentation-proxy-pending-car-rebuild; 32000 elements are at least restored to their correct 1 x 2 x 1 Technic-brick envelope.
Exact car chassis, axle and wheel/tire transforms from pages 7-8 remain hard evidence and were not altered by the visual rebaseline.
The branch has advanced from 51 to 61 instruction-exact transforms using only manual-corroborated unique groups, exact-anchor neighborhoods and corrected existing inventory occurrences.
Page 22 exact cluster includes the chain/pulley/crank mechanism, unique printed central facade, unique Blue 3009, hinge pair and Black 3176 plate-with-hole.
Manual page 4 contributes the complete three-part crocodile: Green 6026 body, 6027 upper jaw and 6028 tail.
The full-set solver remains evidence-gated: CAD can classify and locate candidates but cannot raise exact coverage without manual provenance.
The page-24 3308 false lead remains quarantined: LDD ref 446 belongs to the page-30 gate-web-arch.
World-space convention: one horizontal unit equals one LEGO stud pitch; one brick height is 1.2 world units.
